cues.en: I recently posted a video called object oriented programming is bad in which I made the theoretical case against object oriented programming and why you should really never do it. And a number of people complained about the title suggesting that it was somehow clickbaity,
cues.zh: 我最近发了一个名为《面向对象编程很糟糕》的视频，从理论层面论证了为什么不该用面向对象编程，以及为什么你真的不该这么做。不少人吐槽这个标题，觉得它有点像标题党，

cues.en: but I disagree. I chose the title because I I think it's really true. I have nothing nice to say about object oriented programming. I don't like it. I think it's really been a disaster for the industry.
cues.zh: 但我不这么认为。我起这个标题是因为我觉得它说的就是事实。我对面向对象编程实在说不出一句好话。我不喜欢它，我觉得它对整个行业来说简直是一场灾难。

cues.en: And so to follow-up that argument and see it through, I wanted to present some concrete examples and this one's upping the ante, so it's called Object Oriented Programming is Embarrassing.
cues.zh: 为了把这个论点贯彻到底，我想拿出一些具体的例子，这次我要加大力度，所以标题叫做《面向对象编程令人尴尬》。

cues.en: In this video, I'll have four examples, but they'll be really short, less than 200 lines in each case. Two of them are in Java and two of them are in Ruby, and I'm going to show how if you rewrite them into just a simple procedural style, the resulting code is much better and I'll try and discuss exactly why.
cues.zh: 在这个视频里，我会给出四个例子，代码都很短，每个都不超过 200 行。其中两个是用 Java 写的，另外两个是用 Ruby 写的。我会展示如果把它们重写成简单的过程式风格，代码会好得多，并深入探讨其中的原因。

cues.en: Just to make the comparison fair, for each example I won't change the language, so from Java I'll rewrite it in Java and if it's in Ruby I'll rewrite it in Ruby.
cues.zh: 为了公平对比，每个例子我都不换语言，Java 的就还用 Java 重写，Ruby 的就还用 Ruby 重写。

cues.en: Be clear, I did not trade pick these examples at all, I just basically took the first examples I found on YouTube or Vimeo of some
cues.zh: 先说明一下，我完全没有刻意挑选这些例子，我基本上只是把在 YouTube 或 Vimeo 上随便搜到的

cues.en: speaker giving a talk explaining how object oriented design is supposed to work and how it's gonna make your code better. These are literally the very first code examples I came across when I started looking for them.
cues.zh: 某个演讲者讲解面向对象设计该如何运作、以及它如何改善代码的最初几个例子拿了过来。这真的是我动手找的时候最先看到的几个代码示例。

cues.en: So if you think the examples are unfair, do send in suggestions.
cues.zh: 所以如果你觉得这些例子有失公允，欢迎留言提建议。

cues.en: Also, I would want to follow us up with even longer examples because I know people are not gonna be convinced with just two underlying examples. They're gonna say, Oh, well object oriented programming's virtues don't really come out until you're talking about much larger samples of code because it protects your code from becoming spaghetti when it gets larger and larger.
cues.zh: 另外，后续我还打算用更长的例子来跟进，因为我知道仅凭两百来行的例子是说服不了人的。他们会说：“面向对象编程的优势只有在代码规模大得多的时候才能显现，因为代码越变越大时，它能防止代码变成‘意大利面条’”。

cues.en: Ideally, we would actually put that theory to the test and take a 500,000
cues.zh: 理想情况下，我们应该真正去检验这个理论，找一个 50 万

cues.en: line program and rewrite it from object oriented code into procedural and vice versa and see what we get. For obvious reasons though, no one ever does that, but what I would like to do at least is next take an example of say a thousand or 2,000 lines and then next maybe some example that say 10,000 lines.
cues.zh: 行的程序，把面向对象代码重写为过程式代码，反之亦然，看看最终结果。不过显而易见，没人会真的这么做，但我至少打算下一步找一个一两千行的例子，然后再找一个大概一万行的例子。

cues.en: And ideally,
cues.zh: 理想的话，

cues.en: I don't know,
cues.zh: 我也说不准，

cues.en: rewriting in like 50,000 lines is a lot of work and I don't know if there's an ideal candidate for it, but maybe one could be found. That would that would be a long term project probably.
cues.zh: 重写大概 5 万行的代码工作量太大了，我也不知道能不能找到合适的目标，但也许能找到。那大概会是一个长期项目了。

cues.en: In the meantime, if you have some suggestions of some code example you found, some some GitHub repo of a complete program or maybe even just some submodule of a program that's like 1,000 to 2,000 lines or 10,000 lines, I'd very appreciate if you sent me some suggestions.
cues.zh: 与此同时，如果你能推荐一些你找到的代码示例、某个完整程序的 GitHub 仓库，或者甚至只是某个大概 1000 到 2000 行、或 10000 行的程序子模块，我会非常感激。

cues.en: Preferably, it would be something in Java or JavaScript or Python or Ruby even though I prefer Python.
cues.zh: 最好是 Java、JavaScript、Python 或 Ruby 之类的语言，虽然我更偏爱 Python。

cues.en: It's not a strict requirement, but it's better if it's in language that everyone knows because I I wanna have it be accessible to as many people as possible. So probably preferably JavaScript.
cues.zh: 这倒不是硬性要求，但最好用大家都懂的语言，因为我想让尽可能多的人都能看懂。所以可能最好还是用 JavaScript。

cues.en: Though if it... Make sure it's an example that is actually in an object oriented style, not perfunctory object oriented style, but actual object oriented style.
cues.zh: 不过如果……请确保这个例子是真正的面向对象风格，而不是敷衍了事的面向对象，而是实实在在的面向对象风格。

cues.en: So before getting into the examples, very briefly, I just wanna recap very, very broadly my argument against object oriented programming.
cues.zh: 在进入示例之前，我先非常简略地、从宏观层面上回顾一下我反对面向对象编程的论点。

cues.en: This is a new formulation, I suppose, than what I originally stated in the video, but it's another simple way of thinking about it, and that is just let data be data.
cues.zh: 这个说法可能和我最初在视频里讲的有所不同，但这是理解它的另一种简单方式，那就是：让数据就做数据本身。

cues.en: What object oriented programming demands is that we're supposed to be conceptualizing our data as not just data, but as some sort of thing with responsibilities
cues.zh: 面向对象编程要求我们把数据不仅仅看作数据，而是看作某种负有职责的东西

cues.en: and something which acts in the world. We basically have to,
cues.zh: 以及能在现实世界中行动的事物。我们基本上得

cues.en: imbue our data with intent and agency,
cues.zh: 为我们的数据注入意图和能动性，

cues.en: and that's just a fundamental mistake. Data does not do things. Data is just inert, and that's the way it should be. And you're just adding confusion if you try and conceptualize
cues.zh: 而这根本就是个错误。数据本身不会做任何事。数据只是静态的，而且理应如此。如果你试图把数据概念化成能动的，那只是在添乱

cues.en: your data as some kind of actor.
cues.zh: 把你的数据看作某种 actor。

cues.en: The other side of the coin is that we should let our actions just be actions.
cues.zh: 硬币的另一面是，我们应该让我们的行为就只是行为。

cues.en: We shouldn't have to conceptualize
cues.zh: 我们不该还要费劲去理解这些概念。

cues.en: all the things we want to do in code in terms of some kind of data. We shouldn't have to nounify all our verbs.
cues.zh: 用某种数据来表达我们在代码里想做的一切。我们不该非得把所有动词都名词化。

cues.en: It is this conflation of action with data and vice versa that I think makes object oriented programming so mystifying.
cues.zh: 我认为，正是这种动作与数据概念的混淆（以及数据与动作的混淆），让面向对象编程如此令人费解。

cues.en: If you go down that path, if you follow the advice of the object oriented programming gurus,
cues.zh: 如果你走这条路，遵循面向编程大师们的建议，

cues.en: I think what happens inevitably
cues.zh: 我认为必然会发生的是

cues.en: is that writing code then begins to feel like you're having to solve the problems of analytical philosophy and platonic essentialism.
cues.zh: 也就是说，写代码开始让人觉得，你得去解决分析哲学和柏拉图式本质主义的问题。

cues.en: You have to constantly question
cues.zh: 你得不断去质疑

cues.en: the nature of the entities you are creating in your code. If you create a a chair class, for example, you have to consider the true nature of a chair. You have to
cues.zh: 你在代码中创建的实体的本质。比如，如果你创建一个 chair 类，就必须思考椅子的真正本质。你必须

cues.en: determine its essential aspects because if you get that wrong,
cues.zh: 确定它的关键方面，因为如果你弄错了，

cues.en: according to these gurus, if you draw the boundaries around this entity incorrectly,
cues.zh: 按照这些大师的说法，如果你把这个实体的边界划错了，

cues.en: you're violating some some principle or another of object oriented code.
cues.zh: 你反正就是违反了面向对象代码的某条什么原则。

cues.en: It's gonna bite you in the ass in one way or another and your code's gonna become spaghetti and all the guarantees they promised about what object oriented programming is gonna deliver for you, all their guarantees are void and you can't hold them responsible
cues.zh: 它迟早会以某种方式坑你一把，你的代码会变成一团乱麻，而他们所承诺的面向对象编程能带来的一切，所有保证全都作废，你还怪不到他们头上，

cues.en: because you didn't follow one supposed principle exactly as they intended.
cues.zh: 就因为你没有完全按照他们设想的那样遵循某个所谓的原则。

cues.en: Notice then the justification for object oriented programming is circular. You try and do object oriented designs and they don't seem to really quite work and you don't understand why things are supposed to be arranged in this way and what benefits you're supposed to get. Well, it's because you're just not doing it right, so here are 10 more principles and guidelines.
cues.zh: 注意到了吗，面向对象编程的辩护是循环论证的。你尝试做面向对象设计，发现并不怎么好使，搞不懂为什么非要这么组织代码，能得到什么好处。“哎，那是因为你姿势不对，来，再给你10条原则和规范。”

cues.en: In other words...
cues.zh: 换句话说……

cues.en: So the first example is from a talk given by Sandy Metz called solid object oriented design. You can find it on YouTube.
cues.zh: 第一个例子来自 Sandy Metz 的一场演讲，叫作《SOLID 面向对象设计》，在 YouTube 上能搜到。

cues.en: The centerpiece of the talk is a really short class that processes a patent. It downloads a patent file, it parses the file, and then it updates that patent information in a database.
cues.zh: 这场演讲的核心是一个非常简短的类，用来处理专利。它下载专利文件、解析文件，然后在数据库中更新专利信息。

cues.en: And the core thrust of her talk is she's attempting to demonstrate the so called single responsibility principle, this idea that your classes
cues.zh: 她演讲的核心主旨是试图阐释所谓的“单一职责原则”，即你的类

cues.en: and generally also your methods should only be doing one thing.
cues.zh: 通常也包括你的方法，应该只做一件事。

cues.en: What exactly does it mean for something to be doing just one thing and one thing only?
cues.zh: 但“只做一件事，而且仅此一件”到底是什么意思？

cues.en: Well, that's a disputed point. The definition given by Robert Martin, aka Uncle Bob, who coined the solid principles in SRP, the single responsibility principle, his definition is that a single class, a single unit should have only one reason for change.
cues.zh: 这就存在争议了。提出 SOLID 原则和 SRP（单一职责原则）的 Robert Martin（也就是 Uncle Bob），给出的定义是：一个类，即单个单元，应该只有一个引起它改变的原因。

cues.en: Now, what exactly is one reason for change?
cues.zh: 那么，什么才叫“一个改变的原因”？

cues.en: Well, it's something he explains at length. I think it's... Even after explanation, I think it's a very nebulous idea, which is part of the problem. But putting that aside for the moment, let's look at her example class.
cues.zh: 关于这点他长篇大论地解释过。但我觉得……即便解释过后，这概念依然非常模糊，而这本身就是问题所在。不过先抛开这个不谈，我们来看看她举例的那个类。

cues.en: As you can see, it's written in Ruby, and it has four methods starting with run, which is really where all the action is,
cues.zh: 如你所见，它是用 Ruby 写的，有四个方法，从 run 开始，也就是核心逻辑所在，

cues.en: that invokes the other three methods,
cues.zh: 它会调用另外三个方法：

cues.en: download file, parse, and then update patents.
cues.zh: download file（下载文件）、parse（解析），然后 update patents（更新专利）。

cues.en: Sandy, however, is not satisfied with this design and says that you shouldn't be either because what's going on here is we just have too many responsibilities
cues.zh: 然而 Sandy 对这个设计并不满意，并且说你也不该满意，因为这里的问题在于，我们塞了太多职责

cues.en: in one class.
cues.zh: 在同一个类里。

cues.en: I actually broadly agree on that point. It's very strange that this one unit of code is both downloading files, but then also parsing
cues.zh: 这一点上我其实大体赞同。单单这一个代码单元，既要下载文件，又要负责解析，

cues.en: and updating the database.
cues.zh: 还要更新数据库，确实很奇怪。

cues.en: It's mixing a lot of disparate stuff in this one unit of code that, yes, do all concern patents,
cues.zh: 它在这个代码单元里混杂了许多风马牛不相及的事情，尽管没错，它们确实都和专利有关，

cues.en: I suppose.
cues.zh: 我想确实是。

cues.en: But there is something really weird going on here as evidenced by the simple fact that, you know, classes are supposed to be data types and yet look, there are no fields in this class. So what the hell is this thing really?
cues.zh: 但这里面有个非常诡异的地方，最直接的证据就是：要知道，类本来应该是一种数据类型，但你看，这个类里根本没有任何字段。那这玩意儿到底算个啥？

cues.en: The real answer is that it's just this tiny namespace and that's all that's going on here. That's all this class really is except it's worse than that because in object oriented code to use a class you have to instantiate it, so we have to manage this instance thing in a totally nonsensical way. We're managing this instance that has no persistent value whatsoever
cues.zh: 真正的答案是，它其实就是这么一个微小的命名空间，仅此而已。这个类本质上就这么点东西——甚至更糟，因为在面向对象的代码里，要用一个类就得先实例化它，所以我们不得不用一种完全莫名其妙的方式去管理这个 instance。我们管理的这个 instance，根本没有任何持久的价值。

cues.en: and so it's you immediately dispose of it after invoking the run method. What what is this thing? Why does it have to be a thing? It serves no purpose being a thing.
cues.zh: 所以在调用 run 方法之后你就立即把它销毁了。这……这是个什么东西？为什么非得是个东西？它作为一个东西存在毫无意义。

cues.en: Sandy's prescription is given this nonsensical class, the solution is, as you might expect, more classes.
cues.zh: Sandy 针对这个荒谬的类开出的药方，正如你所料，就是再加更多的类。

cues.en: In her rewrite, she ends up with first this config class,
cues.zh: 在她的重写版本里，她首先得到的是这个配置类，

cues.en: which separates out and effectively generalizes the configuration concerns of this program, which which is a sound idea, I I think.
cues.zh: 它把这个程序的配置关注点分离出来并有效泛化，我认为这是个合理的想法。

cues.en: But we have this constructor, which the initialize method, which takes in some set of options potentially.
cues.zh: 但我们有这个构造函数，也就是 initialize 方法，它可能会接收一组选项。

cues.en: I don't know exactly what purpose they serve, but anyway, so the options tell us where do we get the filename, I believe, for this YAML file that has configuration stuff that's loaded.
cues.zh: 我不太清楚它们具体是干什么用的，不过总之，这些选项告诉我们从哪里获取文件名，我相信就是那个被加载的、包含配置信息的 YAML 文件的文件名。

cues.en: And from the YAML file, we get this data, which is then,
cues.zh: 我们从 YAML 文件中获取这些数据，随后，

cues.en: there's some weird meta business going on here in Ruby. In her defined methods for environment method,
cues.zh: Ruby 里这里有些奇怪的元编程操作。在她为 environment 方法定义的那些方法里，

cues.en: the names are turned into effectively properties of the config class itself or rather actually methods of the config class itself
cues.zh: 这些名称实际上变成了 config 类本身的属性，更准确地说，其实是 config 类本身的方法。

cues.en: that return values
cues.zh: 这些会返回值

cues.en: corresponding to the key value pairs of the configuration file. Effectively, in the end, we get a config instance that has a method for all the configuration
cues.zh: 对应于配置文件中的键值对。实际上，最终我们会得到一个 config 实例，它为所有配置项都提供了相应的方法。

cues.en: property names and you just invoke the method to get its associated value.
cues.zh: 属性名，你只需调用方法就能获取其关联的值。

cues.en: So then my objection to this class is why do we need it at all? Why can't we just have a hash map? Instead of having a constructor, we'd have some function taking in the options, doing all the same business, parsing this YAML file, but why not just return a hash map? Why do we need this class?
cues.zh: 那么我对这类设计提出的异议是：我们到底为什么需要它？为什么不能直接用一个哈希表？我们本来可以不用构造器，而是写一个函数接收这些选项，做完全相同的处理——解析这个 YAML 文件——但为什么不直接返回一个哈希表呢？为什么非要这个类不可？

cues.en: She also moves all of the downloading business into its own class called FTP Downloader,
cues.zh: 她还把所有下载相关的逻辑移到了一个叫 FTPDownloader 的独立类里，

cues.en: and a similar absurdity leaps out here. Why is this a class? We're initializing
cues.zh: 类似的荒谬之处在这里也很明显。为什么这是一个类？我们正在初始化

cues.en: this config property,
cues.zh: 这个配置属性，

cues.en: which we're never gonna use again. Any user of the FTP downloader is never gonna access this config property.
cues.zh: 我们以后再也不会用到它。FTP 下载器的任何用户都不会再访问这个配置属性。

cues.en: It's just they're gonna call this download file method. You're creating a whole instance of a class just to call this one method. Why do we have a class? Why is this not just a function?
cues.zh: 他们只是想调用这个 download file 方法。你为了调用这一个方法，创建了整个类实例。为什么要有类？为什么这不只是一个函数？

cues.en: Lastly, here's a rewrite of the patent job class.
cues.zh: 最后，这是专利任务类的重写版本。

cues.en: The difference is there's now no downloader method. Instead,
cues.zh: 区别在于现在没有 downloader 方法了。取而代之的是，

cues.en: in the constructor, we create a config object and then pass that to create a downloader object,
cues.zh: 在构造函数中，我们创建一个 config 对象，然后用它来创建一个 downloader 对象，

cues.en: and this downloader object is preserved in a downloader field, which is then later used when we call the run method.
cues.zh: 而这个 downloader 对象会保存在 downloader 字段中，之后我们调用 run 方法时就会用到它。

cues.en: And I'll note here, I'm surprised she doesn't use constructor injection. It's odd that she has her patent job actually creating
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，我很惊讶她没有使用构造函数注入。她居然让自己的专利任务实际创建了

cues.en: these config objects and downloader objects.
cues.zh: 这些配置对象和下载器对象。

cues.en: As much as I don't like object oriented programming, if you are going to do it, I think for a very good reason, you do use dependency injection because that... Well, that's a whole tangent, but basically it solves the problem of having to wire together all your objects or at least a much more sane way of doing it. So I'm surprised she doesn't do that here. It seems wrong that she's instantiating these objects inside this other constructor.
cues.zh: 虽然我不太喜欢面向对象编程，但如果出于充分的理由要用它，我认为你应该使用依赖注入，因为它……好吧，这是个很长的题外话，简单来说，它解决了需要手动组装所有对象的问题，或者说提供了一种靠谱得多的做法。所以我很惊讶她在这里没有这么做。在这个构造函数里实例化那些对象，看起来是不对的。

cues.en: Anyway, that's a moot point because the code should just be this. It should just be straight procedural code, just a bunch of kernel methods as they're called in Ruby, basically just functions.
cues.zh: 不过这点其实无关紧要，因为代码本来就应该是这样。它应该是直接的过程式代码，也就是一堆 Ruby 里所谓的 Kernel 方法，基本上就是函数。

cues.en: We don't have to ponder the significance of any classes and and speculate as to what their fields might signify, why they exist, and what purpose they serve. And so say instead of a config class, we just have this get config function which returns a hash with all the fields, parsed out of the YAML file, end of story.
cues.zh: 我们不必去琢磨任何类有什么意义，也不用猜它们的字段可能代表什么、为什么存在、有什么用途。所以与其用配置类，我们只要这个 get config 函数，它返回一个哈希，里面包含从 YAML 文件解析出来的所有字段，就这么简单。

cues.en: We don't have to think about any constructors, and we don't have to do silly things like creating objects immediately calling one method and then never using the object again. We don't have to do silly things like that. In fact, I would go a little further here, I would take these little tiny functions that don't get called anywhere else except in this one place in the process patent function and just put them in line there.
cues.zh:
我们不需要考虑任何构造函数，也不需要做那种愚蠢的事：创建对象，立即调用其中一个方法，然后再也不使用这个对象。
我们不需要做这种蠢事。
实际上，我还想再进一步：把这些只在 process patent 函数的这一处使用、其他地方都不会调用的小函数，直接内联到那里。

cues.en: Maybe speculatively in the future as the program evolves, those might become larger, more involved operations
cues.zh: 或许在未来随着程序不断演进，这些操作会变得更大、更复杂，参与的步骤也更多

cues.en: where
cues.zh: 哪里

cues.en: maybe at some point it'll make sense to split them off into their own functions because they get really involved. But as it stands, it it seems really silly.
cues.zh: 也许到某个时候，把它们拆成独立函数会合理，因为它们会变得非常复杂。但就目前来看，这显得很傻。

cues.en: You know, if I can come across your codebase and encounter just three functions I have to understand instead of five, well, of course, at this tiny scale, it's no big deal either way, so it doesn't really matter, but if you can show me a codebase where instead of a 100 functions, I have three fifths of that, that's just way more tractable. It's just a lot easier to get a foothold and start understanding the code because they don't have to contemplate
cues.zh: 你看，如果我接手一个代码库，只需要理解三个函数，而不是五个，当然，在这么小的规模下，区别其实不大，也没什么影响；但如果原本有 100 个函数，而现在只有五分之三，也就是 60 个，那就更容易处理得多。这样更容易找到切入点，开始理解代码，因为不用去考虑

cues.en: the potential uses of these functions and where they might get called.
cues.zh: 这些函数的潜在用途，以及它们可能会在哪些地方被调用。

cues.en: The next example comes from a video by Derek Banas from a few years ago. It's his whole series he has on object oriented design.
cues.zh: 下一个例子来自 Derek Banas 几年前的一个视频。这是他整套关于面向对象设计的系列课程。

cues.en: There are 11 or so videos, but this code comes from the second one of those. To be fair to Derek, his other videos on programming, his more recent ones I've seen are actually quite good,
cues.zh:
大概有 11 个视频，但这段代码来自其中第二个。
公平地说，Derek 的其他编程视频，我最近看过的那些其实相当不错，

cues.en: but this series is terrible because just the nature of what he's trying to teach. It's just disastrous.
cues.zh: 但这个系列很糟糕，就因为要教的内容本身的性质。简直是一场灾难。

cues.en: So in this example, he is
cues.zh: 所以在这个例子里，他在

cues.en: writing a coin flipping game. Yeah. You know, one person throws a coin into the air and then someone else calls it heads or tails, and there's a winner.
cues.zh: 写一个抛硬币游戏。对，你知道，一个人把硬币抛向空中，另一个人猜正面还是反面，然后就会有一个赢家。

cues.en: It's not gonna be actually really be an interactive program. It's just we're simulating the result to get the end result, you know, so one of two named players wins
cues.zh: 这其实不算真正的交互式程序，只是模拟结果，得出最终结果。你知道，两个指定玩家中有一个会赢，

cues.en: and randomly it's either heads or tails, and that's it. And we just print out so and so one with a coin flip of heads or so and so one with a coin flip of tails, and that's all we're going for here.
cues.zh: 结果随机是正面或反面，就这么简单。我们只要打印出某某人赢了，抛出的结果是正面；或者某某人赢了，抛出的结果是反面。我们要做的就这些。

cues.en: In this video, he's trying to demonstrate how to do formal modeling using
cues.zh: 在这段视频里，他试着演示如何用

cues.en: UML techniques. UML, what does it stand for? Unified Modeling Language,
cues.zh: UML 技术进行形式化建模。UML 是什么的缩写？统一建模语言，

cues.en: universal model, something like that. Who cares? It's fucking garbage.
cues.zh: 通用模型什么的。谁在乎？这玩意儿烂透了。

cues.en: As you can see by this, this is his use case. He has his class diagram. He has his three classes. There's a player and a coin and a coin game.
cues.zh: 你看，这是他的用例图，还有类图。他有三个类：Player、Coin 和 CoinGame。

cues.en: And, you know, the class diagram is one thing, but then there's the actual composition of of instances. So you have an object model, which is different.
cues.zh: 你知道，类图是一回事，实例之间的实际组合又是另一回事。所以还有对象图，那是不同的东西。

cues.en: And then we have a sequence diagram, which is basically just sort of like a a visual representation of of progression of time and and what talks to what.
cues.zh: 然后还有序列图，基本上就是用图形表示时间如何推进，以及对象之间如何交互。

cues.en: And then from all that, he writes his actual code. So we have four classes here. The the fourth class is just a coin flipping game in the bottom right, which is just a container for main because, know, it's Java and everything has to be a class.
cues.zh: 接着，他根据这些图写出实际代码。这里有四个类。第四个类在右下角，就是抛硬币游戏，只是个装 main 的容器，因为这是 Java，什么东西都得是一个类。

cues.en: I'm not even gonna walk through this code. It... It's totally confused even for something so simple because just... Here. This is all he needs. He doesn't really need classes of any kind except for container for main. And then in this main, okay, we'll we'll split out play game to another method, I suppose. Doesn't really matter in this case. We just take in two strings, we randomly pick one of them, and then we randomly pick heads or tails and print out so and so one of... With a flip of whatever.
cues.zh: 我都不想逐行讲这段代码。它……就这么简单的东西，代码也写得一团糟，因为……你看，他只需要这些。除了装 main 的容器，根本不需要任何类。然后在 main 里，好吧，我们可以把 playGame 拆成另一个方法。我想也行，不过这儿其实无所谓。我们只要接收两个字符串，随机选一个，再随机选正面或反面，然后打印某某人赢了……抛出来的是正面还是反面。

cues.en: And that's all we need to do, and then we have this in a a loop because that's what he did.
cues.zh: 我们只要做这些，再把它放进循环里，因为他就是这么写的。

cues.en: He... The user is prompted, do you wanna play again? And you hit something, and and it just goes again. That's all.
cues.zh: 他……程序会问用户还要不要再玩一次。你按点什么，然后它就又来一遍。就这么简单。

cues.en: I don't think I have to actually make the argument about why his code is so absurd. Just look at it, and then look at what he actually just needed to do. At a minimum, the lesson here is that UML is just fucking garbage. Don't ever use it. It's crazy.
cues.zh: 我觉得根本不用解释他的代码为什么这么离谱。看看他的代码，再看看他实际上只需要做什么就行了。至少这个例子说明了一点：UML 烂透了，千万别用。简直离谱。

cues.en: If you wanna plan out your code ahead of time, then, you know, do so to a degree. Of course, just plan out your data structures, write a little bit of pseudocode,
cues.zh: 如果你想提前规划代码，那就适当规划一下。当然，可以先规划数据结构，再写一点伪代码，

cues.en: don't try and diagram anything that never works. It's just a pain in the ass to deal with, all the tools for modeling,
cues.zh: 别费劲画什么图，那玩意儿根本不管用。各种建模工具，

cues.en: the boxes and the arrows and everything, and they're all terrible. And even if they were good, it just... What's stupid about visual representation of code is that past a a very tiny amount of complexity,
cues.zh: 还有那些方框、箭头之类的，全都烂透了。就算工具做得不错，也……代码的图形表示很蠢，因为复杂度只要稍微高一点，

cues.en: you have all these boxes and then you need to draw a bunch of lines between them and very quickly you have so many lines that it's really hard to visually parse. And and why didn't you just write code to begin with? Because code has the the nice virtue of, you know, you have a bunch of functions and they can all just refer to each other by name. It's past a certain point of complexity of things all tied together, it's better represented as just text and named references.
cues.zh: 你就会有一堆方框，还得在它们之间画一大堆线。很快线就多到让人根本看不清。那你为什么不一开始就写代码呢？代码有个很好的优点：你有一堆函数，它们可以直接通过名字相互引用。东西之间相互关联的复杂度一旦超过某个程度，用文本和命名引用来表示就更合适了。

cues.en: That's the main reason why visual languages have never really gone anywhere. It's just a fundamental problem.
cues.zh: 这就是视觉语言一直没真正发展起来的主要原因。这是一个根本性的问题。

cues.en: The next example is another one from Sandy Metz called All the Little Things. I I don't mean to pick on Sandy. It's just I found one of her talks since it was easy to find another.
cues.zh: 下一个例子也来自 Sandy Metz，标题是《All the Little Things》。我不是要针对 Sandy，只是她的演讲比较容易找到，所以又选了一个。

cues.en: In this talk, she presents an example of some ugly code, some ugly branching logic,
cues.zh: 在这场演讲中，她展示了一段丑陋的代码，以及其中难看的分支逻辑，

cues.en: and she demonstrates how this ugly branching can be more cleanly represented with polymorphism.
cues.zh: 并演示了如何用多态更干净地表达这种分支。

cues.en: So looking at this actual code,
cues.zh: 那么，看看这段实际代码，

cues.en: I... This was not a real code example clearly. I think it was an arbitrary example,
cues.zh: 我……这显然不是真实的代码示例。我觉得这只是一个随手编的例子，

cues.en: and these are like random World of Warcraft references apparently.
cues.zh: 而且这些似乎是随机出现的《World of Warcraft》相关内容。

cues.en: And looking at this, I think we can all agree that this is ugly code. You don't want to see code like this. If you're gonna have a lot of complex logic,
cues.zh: 看了这段代码，我想大家都会同意：这代码很难看。没人想看到这样的代码。如果你要处理很多复杂逻辑，

cues.en: it should be complex for a reason and you can very quickly see in a few places that this doesn't need to be so complicated. This can be cleaned up definitely.
cues.zh: 那它应该是有原因的复杂，而且你很快就能看出，其中有几处根本不需要这么复杂。完全可以把它清理得更好。

cues.en: But here's her solution. She puts everything in this class, gilded rose, I don't know... I don't understand what that's supposed to signify, but whatever.
cues.zh: 但这是她的解决方案。她把所有东西都放进了这个 GildedRose 类里。我也不知道……不明白这代表什么，不过算了。

cues.en: And inside, we have this class item
cues.zh: 在里面，我们有一个 Item 类，

cues.en: with a tick method and sort of an abstract class item with an empty tick method.
cues.zh: 它有一个 tick 方法，同时还有一个带空 tick 方法的抽象 Item 类。

cues.en: And then we create three specializations of item. We have normal, Bree, and back stage, each with their own tick methods because what you determined with the original branching code is that we really have four mutually exclusive cases. We have the case where we do nothing,
cues.zh: 然后我们创建 Item 的三个特化类：normal、Bree 和 backstage，每个类都有自己的 tick 方法。因为从原来的分支代码中可以看出，实际上有四种互斥的情况：一种是什么都不做，

cues.en: we had one case where the string was equal to normal, another where it's equal to aged bree, and another where we... It's equal to backstage passes to a TEFL 80 etcetera concert. Again, some kind of World of Warcraft reference there.
cues.zh: 一种是字符串等于 normal，另一种是等于 aged Bree，还有一种是……等于某场 TFL 80 之类音乐会的 backstage passes。这里似乎又是某种《World of Warcraft》梗。

cues.en: So at the bottom here, she has default classes item, but then there's the specific cases. She has this hash map, normal maps, the normal class, h bree to the bree class, and backstage yada yada to the backstage class.
cues.zh: 所以在底部，她有默认的 Item 类，然后是几个具体情况。她用了一个哈希映射：normal 映射到 normal 类，aged Bree 映射到 Bree 类，backstage 之类的值映射到 backstage 类。

cues.en: And then at the bottom, have the self dot four method. I think the significance of self here is that this makes it basically a static method of GildedRose. It's a it's a class method rather than an actual instance method. So you write GildedRose dot four and you pass in the name, which is gonna be a string like normal, and then the the quality and days remaining, and you get back an item object upon which you call its tick method, and you get the same branching behavior we saw in the original code.
cues.zh: 然后在底部有 self.for 方法。我觉得这里使用 self 的意义在于，这基本上让它成为 GildedRose 的静态方法。它是一个类方法，而不是实际的实例方法。所以你可以写 GildedRose.for，传入名称，也就是像 normal 这样的字符串，再传入质量和剩余天数，随后得到一个 Item 对象，然后调用它的 tick 方法，这样就实现了和原始代码中相同的分支行为。

cues.en: So all of this is clever,
cues.zh: 所以这一切都很巧妙，

cues.en: I suppose. It's certainly making full use of Ruby language features.
cues.zh: 我想是这样。至少它充分利用了 Ruby 的语言特性。

cues.en: But if you don't care about doing that, why didn't you just write this code?
cues.zh: 但如果你不想这么做，为什么不直接写成这样呢？

cues.en: The problem with the original code, the reason it was so ugly is because it didn't correctly first identify
cues.zh: 原版代码的问题，也就是它之所以那么难看，是因为它一开始就没有准确识别出

cues.en: the four major mutually exclusive cases.
cues.zh: 那四种主要的互斥情况。

cues.en: And if it had, there's no reason it can't be expressed as a switch or in a Feltz ladder. The way she presents it in the talk is that polymorphism swoops in and saves the day and makes the code much cleaner, but the... There's no need for it. You you can just write a damn switch.
cues.zh: 如果识别出来了，完全可以用 switch 或 if-else 阶梯来表达。她在演讲里的表述，就好像多态横空出世拯救了一切，让代码变得干净得多，但……根本没这个必要。你完全可以直接写个该死的 switch。

cues.en: If you can figure out that the major cases are the string being normal or h three or backstage yada yada, then you can just as easily write this code. You don't have to involve polymorphism.
cues.zh: 如果你能搞清楚主要情况是普通字符串、或者 h3、或者是后台等等，那你同样能轻松写出这段代码。根本用不着搬出多态。

cues.en: Why would you want to introduce more concepts of data types into your code when you don't need them? That's just perverse.
cues.zh: 既然用不着，为什么非要在代码里引入更多的数据类型概念？这完全是自讨苦吃。

cues.en: The procedural code version is just as clean and actually much cleaner because it doesn't involve extraneous
cues.zh: 过程式代码的版本同样很整洁，甚至要干净得多，因为它不包含多余的

cues.en: In fact, I would actually make this a little bit more procedural. Here, we're still using
cues.zh: 事实上，我甚至会把它写得更偏过程式一点。在这里，我们依然在使用

cues.en: instance variables as if this is the method of some class, but in a straight procedural version, we don't really have classes, so we do pass into tick, we pass in a name, and then some object,
cues.zh: 实例变量，就好像这是某个类的方法一样；但如果是纯粹的过程式版本，我们根本没有类，所以会传给 tick 一个名称，再传入某个对象，

cues.en: and then operate upon its members.
cues.zh: 然后操作它的成员。

cues.en: Now, I've seen this polymorphism
cues.zh: 我在别的地方也见过这种

cues.en: can replace all branching idea in other places, and the larger argument generally given is, okay, so in your code, you tend to have a switch over one piece of data and you're gonna have parallel switches in many other places in code. And so it's better to express your switch logic polymorphically
cues.zh: “多态可以取代所有分支”的想法，常见的论据通常是：在代码中，你往往会针对某项数据做 switch 分支，而且在很多其他地方也会有平行的 switch。所以最好用多态来表达 switch 逻辑，

cues.en: because then, especially in a in a static language at least,
cues.zh: 因为这样一来，至少在静态语言中，

cues.en: you would be required by the language to make sure that you have all the methods implemented. In Java, for example, If you implement a interface and you don't implement one of the methods, that's an error. So you're less likely to forget to cover all the parallel cases when you introduce a new case. With straight switches, you might update half the switches and then forget that the other half.
cues.zh: 语言会强制要求你实现所有方法。比如在 Java 中，如果你实现了一个接口却漏掉了某个方法，那就是报错。所以新增情况时，你不太容易漏掉所有的平行分支。而直接用 switch 的话，你可能会更新了一半，却忘了另一半。

cues.en: But, of course, that's in a static language, in a dynamic language like Ruby, if you subclass some abstract class and you fail to override one of its
cues.zh: 但这当然是在静态语言里；像 Ruby 这种动态语言，如果你继承了某个抽象类，却没有重写它的某一个

cues.en: methods, you're not gonna get any language warning whatsoever.
cues.zh: 方法，语言层面根本不会给你任何警告。

cues.en: So it seems like a really weak argument to me in a dynamic language.
cues.zh: 所以在动态语言里，我觉得这个论点根本站不住脚。

cues.en: Regardless, I still think polymorphic branching is a perverse idea, mostly because I think these neatly parallel switches are actually quite rare.
cues.zh: 退一步说，我依然觉得用多态做分支是个很别扭的想法，主要是因为那种整齐平行的 switch 实际上非常罕见。

cues.en: Much more commonly, I think you have scenarios where the switches are semi parallel, like they they switch over one set of factors in one part of code, but then the branching logic needs to be quite different in other parts of code.
cues.zh: 更常见的情况是，各种 switch 只是半平行的，比如在代码的某处是基于这一组因素来分支，但在其他地方，分支逻辑可能就大不相同了。

cues.en: So going through all this trouble to reconceptualize
cues.zh: 所以说，费这么大功夫去重新理解

cues.en: certain switches as being switching over types when you don't necessarily have different types, that's a lot of bother and conceptual overhead for something that's quite likely to not pay off in the long run.
cues.zh: 把某些 switch 当作是在不同类型之间做切换，可你实际上未必真的有不同的类型，这么做既麻烦又带来很重的概念负担，而长远来看很可能根本不值得。

cues.en: The last example is from a talk by Robert C. Martin, aka Uncle Bob, who is probably the preeminent object oriented guru.
cues.zh: 最后一个例子来自 Robert C. Martin（人称 Uncle Bob）的演讲，他大概是最顶尖的面向对象大师。

cues.en: And in this talk, he presents a program that parses command line arguments into a more convenient data structure such as, say, you can query, hey,
cues.zh: 在这次演讲中，他展示了一个程序，它把命令行参数解析成更方便的数据结构，比如，你可以查询，嘿，

cues.en: what is the value of the flag that starts with hyphen b or hyphen c, hyphen, some character, right?
cues.zh: 以 -b 或 -c（也就是连字符加某个字符）开头的那个标志，它的值是什么，对吧？

cues.en: And these arguments are specified with a schema string
cues.zh: 而这些参数是用 schema 字符串来指定的

cues.en: in this format here, they're separated by commas
cues.zh: 在这个格式里，它们用逗号分隔

cues.en: and
cues.zh: 和

cues.en: if it's a boolean, it's not marked by any special character, but if it's an integer, it's marked with a number sign and if it's a string, then it's marked with an asterisk.
cues.zh: 如果是布尔值，不用任何特殊字符标记；如果是整数，就用井号标记；如果是字符串，则用星号标记。

cues.en: And so here, for example, this schema string expects an in flag J, a boolean flag F, and a string flag W.
cues.zh: 所以这里举个例子，这个 schema 字符串期望一个 int 标志 J、一个布尔标志 F 和一个字符串标志 W。

cues.en: So given the schema, if say we then had actual command line arguments of
cues.zh: 那么给定这个 schema，假设我们接下来有实际的命令行参数，比如

cues.en: hyphen J 35 and then hyphen W blah blah blah, then the flag j will have the value 35, the flag f will have the value false because there was no f flag,
cues.zh: 连字符 J 35，然后连字符 W blah blah blah，那么标志 j 的值会是 35，标志 f 的值会是 false，因为没有 f 标志，

cues.en: and then flag w will have the value blah blah blah.
cues.zh: 然后，标志 w 的值将是 blah blah blah。

cues.en: So first he presents a version of his code which he thinks is not so great, but then he cleans it up and this is that version. I won't I won't bother showing the bad version. It didn't seem any worse or better than the... This better version, this ostensibly better version, so I'll just show the better version.
cues.zh: 所以一开始，他展示了一个自己觉得不太好的代码版本，后来又把它整理了一遍，这就是整理后的版本。我就不展示那个糟糕的版本了。它看起来并不比这个版本更差或更好……所以我就直接展示这个更好的、至少表面上更好的版本。

cues.en: So what does he have here? First, he has this abstract argument marshaller class with two abstract methods, set and get.
cues.zh: 那么，他这里有什么呢？首先，他有一个抽象的参数封送类，其中包含两个抽象方法：set 和 get。

cues.en: I don't know why he's using an abstract class rather than an interface because there's no, you know, there's no actual fields here, so why why have an abstract class and not an interface?
cues.zh: 我不知道他为什么用抽象类而不是接口，因为这里并没有，呃，并没有实际的字段，所以为什么用抽象类而不是接口呢？

cues.en: Whatever.
cues.zh: 随便吧。

cues.en: That then gets extended into three concrete classes. There's Boolean argument marshaler,
cues.zh: 然后它被扩展成三个具体类。其中有 Boolean argument marshaler，

cues.en: there's also then
cues.zh: 另外还有 then

cues.en: string argument marshaler
cues.zh: 字符串参数编组器

cues.en: and integer argument marshaler and their bodies are really similar. They're they're doing the same stuff except they're dealing with boolean string and integer values and that's the main difference there.
cues.zh: 整数参数封送器和它们的主体其实非常相似。它们做的是同样的事情，只不过处理的是布尔值、字符串和整数值，这就是它们的主要区别。

cues.en: And then those three concrete classes are utilized in this args class, which is where he has his main,
cues.zh: 然后这三个具体类在这个 Args 类中被使用，而这里就是他放 main 方法的地方，

cues.en: so I'm not gonna step through any of the codes, so just look at the bottom right where we have main and so we instantiate args, we pass in a schema string and then also the actual arguments to the main function.
cues.zh: 所以我不逐行讲代码，只看右下角的 main，我们实例化 args，传入一个 schema 字符串，再把实际参数传给 main 函数。

cues.en: That gets us back this args data structure which we can then query with methods get boolean, get int, and get string, and so here we're asking, hey, what is the value of the boolean flag L? And we get back a boolean value and so forth, and then so we parse all of our arguments and get their values and then we pass them off to this execute application method, which doesn't actually... It's not implemented, it's just hypothetically here's your actual program start.
cues.zh: 这样我们就回到了这个 args 数据结构，然后可以用 get boolean、get int 和 get string 方法查询它。这里我们是在问：布尔标志 L 的值是什么？返回的就是一个布尔值，其他方法同理。接着，我们解析所有参数，获取它们的值，再把这些值传给 execute application 方法。这个方法实际上……还没有实现，这里只是设想它作为真正的程序入口。

cues.en: And notice that the args instantiation and its get boolean, get int, and get string methods are all called inside this try block because they can all throw args exceptions.
cues.zh: 注意，args 的实例化，以及它的 get boolean、get int 和 get string 方法，全都在这个 try 代码块中调用，因为它们都可能抛出 args 异常。

cues.en: Now, if you want, take a few moments and study his code and try and figure out what's going on. He does a few really odd things because all he really needs to do is this. There's my solution. I just have a single class args with the the same main function down at the bottom, I'll show on the next slide.
cues.zh: 现在，如果你愿意，可以花点时间研究一下他的代码，试着弄清楚它在做什么。他做了几件很奇怪的事，因为实际上他只需要这样做。这就是我的解决方案：我只用了一个 args 类，并在底部放了同样的 main 函数，下一张幻灯片会展示它。

cues.en: But first,
cues.zh: 不过首先，

cues.en: args has three fields. It has a hash map for characters to integers, a hash map for characters to strings, and a hash map for characters to booleans.
cues.zh: args 有三个字段：一个将字符映射到整数的哈希表，一个将字符映射到字符串的哈希表，以及一个将字符映射到布尔值的哈希表。

cues.en: And then in the constructor we pass in just like his args, we pass in the schema string and the actual args strings. And first what we do is we parse the schema in this loop, we we split the schema string by comma and then for each element of the schema
cues.zh: 然后在构造函数中，和他的 args 一样，我们传入 schema 字符串和实际的 args 字符串。首先，我们在这个循环中解析 schema：按逗号拆分 schema 字符串，然后针对其中的每个元素

cues.en: we add that character to the appropriate hash map given the symbol character that might accompany it.
cues.zh: 根据它后面可能跟着的符号字符，把这个字符加入相应的哈希表。

cues.en: And for for now we're just giving the integer and string and boolean values in these hash maps default values. For boolean,
cues.zh: 现在，我们先给这些哈希表中的整数、字符串和布尔值设置默认值。对于布尔值，

cues.en: default value is false, but then for string and integer the default value is null because it makes sense for boolean flag if you omit the flag then presumably then it should be false, but if you omit a string or integer flag,
cues.zh: 默认值是 false；但对于字符串和整数，默认值是 null。因为如果省略布尔标志，默认设为 false 是合理的；但如果省略字符串或整数标志，

cues.en: who knows what that should be, so there's not really a default value there.
cues.zh: 那谁知道应该是什么值呢？所以它们实际上没有默认值。

cues.en: In any case, our args constructor then continues and we loop through all the actual argument strings
cues.zh: 无论如何，args 构造函数接着会遍历所有实际的参数字符串

cues.en: and we check first if they begin with a hyphen because if they don't begin with a hyphen we don't care about them, just ignore them. But if we do, then we check the next letter and we see, well, is that in the booleans map or the strings map or the ints map and whichever one it's in, we wanna take the specified value and assign it to that character in the hash map. Understand in the default case here in the else clause, if we encounter a character which we didn't see in the schema, then that's an exception. You're not supposed to... We're not supposed to have any such flags if they weren't in the schema.
cues.zh: 我们首先检查它们是否以连字符开头。如果不是，我们就不关心它们，直接忽略。但如果是，就检查下一个字母，看看它是在 booleans 映射、strings 映射，还是 ints 映射中。无论它属于哪一个，我们都要取出指定的值，并把它赋给哈希表中对应的字符。注意，在这里的默认分支，也就是 else 子句中，如果遇到一个 schema 中没有出现过的字符，就会抛出异常。按理说……如果某个标志不在 schema 中，我们就不应该有这样的标志。

cues.en: So that constructor gets us our fully parsed data structure and then just to use the thing, we have the same methods that he has in his code, we have get bool, get string, and get int. And the main function here is exactly what he had. But actually what I would do is probably I wouldn't have get bool, get string, and get int. I would just make the hash map fields public and then access them directly,
cues.zh: 这个构造函数帮我们得到了完整解析好的数据结构，然后要使用它的话，我们有和他的代码里相同的方法：get bool、get string 和 get int。这里的 main 函数和他写的完全一样。不过实际上如果是我来做，我大概不会搞 get bool、get string 和 get int 这三个方法，而是直接把哈希表的字段设为 public，然后直接访问，

cues.en: and I prefer explicit error handling over exceptions, so the resultant code would look something like this.
cues.zh: 而且比起异常我更喜欢显式的错误处理，所以最终代码大概会长这样。

cues.en: We get args dot ints dot get, but that might be null and if so, then we... That's an error. Otherwise, if it's not null, then we can get us a value. And yeah, this is a little ugly and verbose, but that's mainly just because Java has obnoxious
cues.zh: 我们调用 args 点 ints 点 get，但结果可能是 null，如果是 null，那……这就是个错误。否则如果不是 null，我们就能拿到值。确实，这有点丑而且啰嗦，但这主要是因为 Java 在基本类型和对象类型之间有烦人的

cues.en: distinction between primitives and object types,
cues.zh: 区分，

cues.en: so that's really the root problem here.
cues.zh: 这才是这里问题的根源。

cues.en: So, yeah, this is a little verbose being explicit about errors, but I still think it's better to be explicit.
cues.zh: 所以，是的，显式处理错误是有点啰嗦，但我还是觉得显式更好。

cues.en: So let's step back and look at the differences here. In my version of the code, we had an args data type, it had its constructor,
cues.zh: 我们退一步看看两者的差异。在我这版代码里，有一个 args 数据类型，有它的构造函数，

cues.en: and there was the main method. And that's the entire surface level of the code. If you wanna understand what's going in my code,
cues.zh: 还有一个 main 方法。这就是代码的全部表层内容。如果你想理解我的代码在干什么，

cues.en: no question whatsoever where you need to start.
cues.zh: 从哪儿入手完全不需要犹豫。

cues.en: In Uncle Bob's code, have not just one class, we have five. One of them is abstract, which itself is mystifying in its own special way.
cues.zh: 而在 Uncle Bob 的代码里，不止一个类，我们有五个。其中一个是抽象类，它本身就以一种独特的方式令人费解。

cues.en: He has this strange notion of marshallers. I I still can't figure out what that's really supposed to mean.
cues.zh: 他有一种奇怪的"marshaller"（编组器）概念，我到现在还是搞不清这到底想表达什么。

cues.en: And what's oddest of all is that these marshaller classes are all recursive.
cues.zh: 最奇怪的是，这些 marshaller 类全都是递归的。

cues.en: Boolean argument marshaller has a boolean value field, but then also this boolean args field is a map of characters to other argument marshallers.
cues.zh: Boolean argument marshaller 有一个 boolean value 字段，但这个 boolean args 字段又是一个从字符映射到其他 argument marshaller 的映射表。

cues.en: I don't know why he made it the the parent class argument marshaller because it turns out in practice it's always specifically a boolean argument marshaller, so I don't know what's going on there. But I don't know why it's recursive to begin with, it's very, very strange.
cues.zh: 我不明白他为什么把它做成父类 argument marshaller，因为实际上它总是特指 boolean argument marshaller，所以我不知道这里在搞什么。而且我也不明白它为什么一开始就是递归的，非常非常奇怪。

cues.en: I think what happened is that because he was programming in an object oriented style, he just didn't have the clarity to see how simple what he was doing really was,
cues.zh: 我想发生的事情是，因为他用面向对象的风格编程，他根本看不清自己做的事情其实有多简单，

cues.en: and so he couldn't then devise a sensibly simple solution.
cues.zh: 所以他也无法设计出一个合理而简单的方案。

cues.en: When someone comes to his code and they wanna make heads or tails of it, they have to ponder why he has these five different data types and what purposes they really serve. And then looking at the fields, why are these data structures recursive? And then you have to look at all the methods and everything's split up into tiny little methods.
cues.zh: 当有人来看他的代码，想弄明白它到底在干什么时，他们得琢磨为什么有这五个不同的数据类型、它们到底起什么作用。然后看字段，这些数据结构为什么是递归的？接着还得看所有方法，而一切都被拆成了零碎的小方法。

cues.en: So, yes, in the straightforward procedural version, there's a little bit of complex logic as you can see in the loop and branching,
cues.zh: 所以，没错，在直白的过程式版本中，正如你在循环和分支里看到的，有一点复杂逻辑，

cues.en: but his version just chops it up and obscures it. It scatters it all to the winds.
cues.zh: 但他的版本只是把它切碎并加以掩盖，把所有东西都分散开来。

cues.en: If you think simply in terms of data and data transformation
cues.zh: 如果你只从数据和数据转换的角度来思考

cues.en: rather than trying to conceptualize your data as doers
cues.zh: 而不是把数据概念化为执行者

cues.en: and your your actions as somehow also being data types, if you avoid that confusion,
cues.zh: 也不要把操作本身误认为某种数据类型，避免这种混淆，

cues.en: it's much much easier to arrive at straightforward solutions like I did where I just have this Rx class with the three HashMaps.
cues.zh: 就会更容易得出像我这样直截了当的解决方案：只需要一个带有三个 HashMap 的 Rx 类。

cues.en: Because what was the task at hand? I had this array of strings and I just wanted to convert it into a form of data that was more convenient to query, just a form of data that was more convenient to use down the line. That's all I was doing.
cues.zh: 因为当时的任务是什么？我有一个字符串数组，只想把它转换成一种更方便查询的数据形式，也就是一种便于后续使用的数据形式。仅此而已。

cues.en: By avoiding all of his object oriented nonsense, we can have that clarity.
cues.zh: 避开他那些面向对象的繁琐做法，我们就能保持这种清晰性。

cues.en: This brings to mind another talk by Sandy Metz where she explicitly concedes that object oriented code is generally less comprehensible than procedural code, but she defends object oriented code with the idea that you're not supposed to understand the entirety of your code. If you properly decompose everything into this system of little objects,
cues.zh: 这让我想起 Sandy Metz 的另一场演讲，她明确承认面向对象代码通常不如过程式代码容易理解，但她为面向对象代码辩护的理由是：你本来就不需要理解整个代码库。如果你把所有东西恰当地分解成这样一个个小对象，

cues.en: then you can make changes to your code by just adding in more objects without having to fully understand all the connections between them and all the interactions.
cues.zh: 那么修改代码时，只需要添加更多对象，不必完全理解它们之间的所有连接和交互。

cues.en: Aside from being skeptical that this is actually true, that you actually get that benefit in object oriented code, that you can proceed without really understanding your code, I think this is fundamentally just the wrong way to program. Yes, you do need to understand your code and beyond that, you need to understand your tools and you need to understand your environment, meaning generally your platform.
cues.zh: 除了我怀疑面向对象代码真的能带来这种好处，也就是让你不必真正理解代码就能继续开发之外，我认为这从根本上就是错误的编程方式。没错，你确实需要理解自己写的代码；除此之外，还需要理解你的工具和环境，也就是通常所说的平台。

cues.en: When we give up on understanding what we're actually doing when we write code, it just leads to bad software.
cues.zh: 当我们放弃理解自己编写代码时到底在做什么，最终只会导致糟糕的软件。
